edit.description: the one writer passes the shipThrew it already holds

summary: The `not-shipped` prior-attempt record says whether the `shipped` hook threw or returned `false`

per.section: Prior-outcome feedback to the retrying tick

acceptance: A record written after a throwing `shipped` hook is distinguishable on `TickContext.priorAttempts` from one written after a returned `false`, and the rendered block says which.
tests: a not-shipped record distinguishes a thrown shipped hook from a returned false
notes: `buildNotShipped` (src/priorAttempts.ts) takes the sha and footprint only; its one writer (src/Dispatcher.ts, the ship decision) already holds `shipThrew` and puts it on the verdict's merge outcome. Still no reason vocabulary: which of the two happened is the engine's own fact, never the chain's why.

summary: Let a consumer declare `agents[phase].inheritUserMcp`, passed through to that phase's `claudeCode` options
acceptance: A declaration setting `inheritUserMcp` loads and constructs that phase's agent with it; omitting it leaves the engine's default (off).
tests: a declared agents inheritUserMcp reaches the phase's claudeCode options
notes: The engine half shipped: `ClaudeCodeOptions.inheritUserMcp`, `--strict-mcp-config` on the argv by default (src/Agent.ts, `.claude/rules/platform-facts.md`). The harness's strict `agents` schema takes model and extraArgs only, so a consumer wanting its own MCP servers has no spelling and the strict schema refuses the field.

edit.description: RenderRefusedAttempt and its failures field: both writers, not spans alone

summary: `RenderRefusedAttempt`'s shipped doc names both producers — a failing inline-exec span and a pre-invocation hook that threw

per.section: Prior-outcome feedback to the retrying tick

acceptance: The exported type's comment and its `failures` field describe both writers; nothing on the shipped `.d.ts` reads as spans-only.
notes: `persistHookRefusal` (src/Dispatcher.ts) writes the record for a `shouldRun`/`promptArgs` throw, and `buildRenderRefused`'s own comment names both; the exported type still reads 'one or more inline-exec spans ... did not resolve', with `failures` as 'every failing span's command text'. Doc comment on the shipped `.d.ts` — the ladder's one carve-out (`engineering.md`).

edit.description: checkoutAt's refusal paragraph: the gate-time contract, not an unexported escape hatch

summary: Trade `checkoutAt`'s doc-comment escape hatch for the gate-time contract the package ships

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

acceptance: The comment on `api.git.checkoutAt` names no route the package does not export; the refusal reads as gate-time by design, per `spec/harness.md`, *The runner interface*.
notes: `addWorktree`/`removeWorktree` (`src/git.ts`) are on neither `src/index.ts` nor `FlumeApi.git`, and `exports` reaches only `.` and `./harness` — the comment rides the shipped `.d.ts` and points at a route no consumer can take. `spec/harness.md` now rules the operation gate-time (0f9dfc8). `{@link}`s to internal symbols are TSDoc-normal and stay. Runtime unaffected: `namedLinesGate` runs through `runGate`, which opens the scope.

edit.description: shrink the Harness-managed state roster to a pointer

summary: Shrink the chain guide's **Harness-managed state** roster to a pointer at `spec/jobs.md`, *Runtime ignores*

per.section: Derived state is computed, never restated beside its source

acceptance: The paragraph names no line of the ignore set and cites the section that owns it; the `plan/pending.json`/`Chain.pendingPath` and `sessions/` claims still read standing alone.
notes: Ruled a copy this tick. The roster spells nine of ten `RUNTIME_IGNORES` names plus `plan/pending.json`, never ignored, and omits `node_modules/`, which is. Sibling of the `job new` bullet `CHAIN-AUTHORING-IGNORES-POINT-AT-THE-SPEC` shrank 45 lines below, which left this one standing pending the ruling. Pinning is off the table outside the `.d.ts` carve-out, so removing the copy is the whole fix.
